# nish/temporal

Dates, times, instants and durations in the ISO 8601 calendar, under the names and the rules of TC39's `Temporal` (`docs/wp64-temporal.md`).

```ts
import {
  Duration,
  Instant,
  PlainDate,
  PlainDateTime,
  PlainTime,
  durationCompare,
  durationFrom,
  durationFromOrNull,
  instantCompare,
  instantFrom,
  instantFromEpochMilliseconds,
  instantFromOrNull,
  nowInstant,
  plainDateCompare,
  plainDateFrom,
  plainDateFromOrNull,
  plainDateTimeCompare,
  plainDateTimeFrom,
  plainDateTimeFromOrNull,
  plainTimeCompare,
  plainTimeFrom,
  plainTimeFromOrNull,
  tryPlainDate,
  tryPlainDateFrom,
} from "nish/temporal";
```

<scalar-code-group>

```ts example.ts
import { PlainDate, Duration, plainDateFrom } from "nish/temporal";

export const main = (): i32 => {
  const due: PlainDate = plainDateFrom("2024-01-31");
  const next: PlainDate = due.add(new Duration(0, 1));   // 2024-02-29
  console.log(next.toString());
  console.log(due.until(next).toString());              // P29D
  return 0;
};
```

</scalar-code-group>

<scalar-detail title="Five types, each immutable">

`PlainDate`, `PlainTime` and `PlainDateTime`
are wall-clock values with no time zone; `Instant` is an exact point on the
UTC timeline; `Duration` is ten signed fields, `years` to `nanoseconds`.
Every method answers a new value. A field reads as Temporal's getter of the
same name does (`d.year`, `d.dayOfWeek`, `t.nanosecond`), and the string
forms are Temporal's byte for byte.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="What is Temporal's and what is this module's">

A class here is the
Temporal class of the same name, and `plainDateFrom(s)` is
`Temporal.PlainDate.from(s)`, `plainDateCompare(a, b)` is
`Temporal.PlainDate.compare(a, b)`, and so on for each type: Nish has no
`static` members, so the class's statics are free functions named after it.
The arithmetic follows the specification's: `add` constrains a day past the
end of the month (`2024-01-31` plus a month is `2024-02-29`), `until` and
`since` answer the largest unit Temporal's default does (days for a date or a
date-time, hours for a time, seconds for an instant), and a string Temporal
refuses with a `RangeError` panics here with a message that starts
`RangeError:`. The `...OrNull` functions are this module's own: the same
parse, answering `null` instead.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="What is not here yet">

**What is not here yet** (`docs/wp64-temporal.md` §6): `ZonedDateTime` and
every time zone but UTC, `PlainYearMonth`, `PlainMonthDay`, the option
bags (`{ largestUnit: "year" }`, `with({ day: 1 })`, `round`, `total`),
calendars other than `iso8601`, `toLocaleString`, and `epochNanoseconds`,
which is a `bigint` in JavaScript. An `Instant` is any nanosecond in
Temporal's range of ±10^8 days from 1970, held as `i64` seconds and `i32`
nanoseconds; a `Duration`'s fields are `i64`, which is narrower than
Temporal's for microseconds and nanoseconds alone.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Private helpers carry the module's name">

**Private helpers carry the module's name** because they share the
importing program's flat symbol namespace (`docs/wp26-stdlib.md` §3e).

</scalar-detail>

## Functions

### durationCompare

`Temporal.Duration.compare(a, b)`: -1, 0 or 1 as `a` is shorter than, as
long as, or longer than `b`, each day counted as 24 hours. Panics with a
`RangeError` when either has years, months or weeks, which Temporal
compares only against a `relativeTo` date; two durations with the same
fields compare equal whatever they hold.

```ts
const durationCompare: (a: Duration, b: Duration) => i32
```

<scalar-field name="a" type="Duration" required>

the first duration

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="b" type="Duration" required>

the second duration

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

the order of the two

</scalar-field>

### durationFrom

`Temporal.Duration.from(text)`: the duration an ISO 8601 string names,
`[+-]P[nY][nM][nW][nD][T[nH][nM][nS]]` in either case, where the last time
field may have a fraction of up to nine digits (`PT1.5H` is an hour and 30
minutes). Panics with a `RangeError` on anything else.

```ts
const durationFrom: (text: string) => Duration
```

<scalar-field name="text" type="string" required>

such as `P1Y2M`, `PT36H` or `-P1DT0.5S`

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Duration">

the duration

</scalar-field>

### instantFrom

`Temporal.Instant.from(text)`: the instant an RFC 9557 string names. It
must have a date, a time and either `Z` or a numeric offset, which is
subtracted (`2024-01-15T09:05+01:00` is `2024-01-15T08:05:00Z`); a
bracketed time zone after it is ignored. Panics with a `RangeError` on
anything else.

```ts
const instantFrom: (text: string) => Instant
```

<scalar-field name="text" type="string" required>

such as `2024-01-15T09:05:00Z`

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Instant">

the instant

</scalar-field>

### instantFromEpochMilliseconds

`Temporal.Instant.fromEpochMilliseconds(ms)`: the instant `ms` milliseconds
after 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z. Panics with a `RangeError` when `ms` is not a
whole number or is outside ±8.64 × 10^15.

```ts
const instantFromEpochMilliseconds: (ms: f64) => Instant
```

<scalar-field name="ms" type="f64" required>

milliseconds since the epoch

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Instant">

the instant

</scalar-field>

### plainTimeFrom

`Temporal.PlainTime.from(text)`: the time an RFC 9557 string names, either
a time alone (`12:30`, `T1230`, `12:30:15.5`) or a date-time, whose date is
ignored. A string with no time, one with a `Z`, and a time alone without
its `T` that would also read as a year and month or a month and day
(`2021-12`, `1214`) are refused, as Temporal refuses them. Panics with a
`RangeError` on anything else.

```ts
const plainTimeFrom: (text: string) => PlainTime
```

## Classes

### Duration

A length of time in ten signed fields: `Temporal.Duration`. A duration is
not balanced: `PT90M` keeps its 90 minutes. Every non-zero field has the
same sign.

```ts
class Duration
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new Duration(years: i64 = 0, months: i64 = 0, weeks: i64 = 0, days: i64 = 0, hours: i64 = 0, minutes: i64 = 0, seconds: i64 = 0, milliseconds: i64 = 0, microseconds: i64 = 0, nanoseconds: i64 = 0)` | The duration, as `new Temporal.Duration(...)`; every field defaults to 0. Panics with a `RangeError` when two fields have different signs, when `years`, `months` or `weeks` reaches 2^32, or when the rest comes to 2^53 seconds or more. |
| `readonly blank: boolean` | Whether every field is zero. |
| `readonly days: i64` | Days. |
| `readonly hours: i64` | Hours. |
| `readonly microseconds: i64` | Microseconds. |
| `readonly milliseconds: i64` | Milliseconds. |
| `readonly minutes: i64` | Minutes. |
| `readonly months: i64` | Months. |
| `readonly nanoseconds: i64` | Nanoseconds. |
| `readonly seconds: i64` | Seconds. |
| `readonly sign: i32` | -1, 0 or 1: the sign every non-zero field shares. |
| `readonly weeks: i64` | Weeks. |
| `readonly years: i64` | Years. |
| `abs(): Duration` | This duration with every field made non-negative. |
| `add(other: Duration): Duration` | The sum of this duration and `other`, balanced up to the larger of the two's largest non-zero unit, as Temporal's `Duration.prototype.add` balances it (`P1D` plus `PT25H` is `P2DT1H`). Panics with a `RangeError` when either has years, months or weeks, whose length depends on a date. |
| `negated(): Duration` | This duration with every field's sign flipped. |
| `subtract(other: Duration): Duration` | This duration minus `other`: `add` of its negation. |
| `toJSON(): string` | The same string as `toString`. |
| `toString(): string` | The duration as ISO 8601 writes it: `P1Y2M3W4DT5H6M7.008S`, `-PT90M`, and `PT0S` when blank. The seconds and their fractions are written as one decimal number, so `PT1.5S` reads back as 1 second and 500 milliseconds. |

### Instant

An exact point on the UTC timeline, to the nanosecond: `Temporal.Instant`.
It has no calendar and no time zone; `toString` writes it in UTC.

```ts
class Instant
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new Instant(epochSeconds: i64, nanoseconds: i64 = 0)` | The instant `epochSeconds` seconds and `nanoseconds` nanoseconds after the epoch. This is this module's constructor, not Temporal's, whose `new Temporal.Instant(epochNanoseconds)` takes a `bigint`; use `instantFromEpochMilliseconds` or `instantFrom` for a portable program. Panics with a `RangeError` outside ±10^8 days of the epoch. |
| `readonly epochMilliseconds: f64` | Milliseconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z, rounded toward negative infinity. |
| `add(duration: Duration): Instant` | This instant moved by `duration`, which may hold hours and smaller units only: a day is not always 24 hours once a zone is involved, so Temporal refuses days and larger units here, and so does this, with a `RangeError`. |
| `equals(other: Instant): boolean` | Whether `other` is the same instant. |
| `since(other: Instant): Duration` | The time from `other` to this instant: `other.until(this)`. |
| `subtract(duration: Duration): Instant` | This instant moved back by `duration`: `add` of its negation. |
| `toJSON(): string` | The same string as `toString`. |
| `toString(): string` | The instant in UTC as Temporal writes it: `2024-01-15T09:05:00Z`, with the fraction of the second to as many digits as it needs. |
| `until(other: Instant): Duration` | The time from this instant to `other` in seconds and smaller units (Temporal's default `largestUnit: "second"`). |

### PlainDate

A calendar date with no time and no time zone: `Temporal.PlainDate` in the
ISO 8601 calendar. Every field is Temporal's getter of the same name.

```ts
class PlainDate
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new PlainDate(isoYear: i32, isoMonth: i32, isoDay: i32)` | The date `isoYear-isoMonth-isoDay`, as `new Temporal.PlainDate(y, m, d)`. Panics with a `RangeError` when the fields name no date, or one outside Temporal's range of -271821-04-19 to +275760-09-13. |
| `readonly calendarId: string` | The calendar, always `iso8601`. |
| `readonly day: i32` | The day of the month, from 1. |
| `readonly dayOfWeek: i32` | The weekday, 1 for Monday to 7 for Sunday. |
| `readonly dayOfYear: i32` | The day of the year, 1 for 1 January. |
| `readonly daysInMonth: i32` | Days in this date's month. |
| `readonly daysInWeek: i32` | Days in a week: 7. |
| `readonly daysInYear: i32` | Days in this date's year: 365 or 366. |
| `readonly inLeapYear: boolean` | Whether this date's year is a leap year. |
| `readonly month: i32` | The month, 1 to 12. |
| `readonly monthCode: string` | The month as Temporal codes it: `M01` to `M12`. |
| `readonly monthsInYear: i32` | Months in a year: 12. |
| `readonly weekOfYear: i32` | The ISO week number, 1 to 53. |
| `readonly year: i32` | The year; negative before 1 BCE's year 0. |
| `readonly yearOfWeek: i32` | The year the ISO week belongs to, which differs from `year` near New Year. |
| `add(duration: Duration): PlainDate` | This date moved by `duration`: its years and months first, with a day past the end of the new month moved back to its last day (Temporal's `overflow: "constrain"`), then its weeks and days, then whole days of its time fields. Panics with a `RangeError` when the answer is outside Temporal's range. |
| `equals(other: PlainDate): boolean` | Whether `other` is the same date. |
| `since(other: PlainDate): Duration` | The days from `other` to this date: `other.until(this)`. |
| `subtract(duration: Duration): PlainDate` | This date moved back by `duration`: `add` of its negation. |
| `toJSON(): string` | The same string as `toString`, which is what `JSON.stringify` writes. |
| `toPlainDateTime(time: PlainTime): PlainDateTime` | This date at `time`. |
| `toString(): string` | The date as Temporal writes it: `2024-01-15`, or `+012345-01-15` for a year past 9999 or before 0. |
| `tryAdd(duration: Duration): Result<PlainDate, string>` | `add`, answering an answer outside Temporal's range as `Err` where `add` panics. Not part of Temporal. |
| `until(other: PlainDate): Duration` | The days from this date to `other`, as a duration of days alone (Temporal's default `largestUnit: "day"`); negative when `other` is earlier. |

### PlainDateTime

A date and a time of day with no time zone: `Temporal.PlainDateTime` in the
ISO 8601 calendar. It has every field of `PlainDate` and of `PlainTime`.

```ts
class PlainDateTime
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new PlainDateTime(isoYear: i32, isoMonth: i32, isoDay: i32, hour: i32 = 0, minute: i32 = 0, second: i32 = 0, millisecond: i32 = 0, microsecond: i32 = 0, nanosecond: i32 = 0)` | The date-time, as `new Temporal.PlainDateTime(...)`; the time fields default to 0. Panics with a `RangeError` on a field out of range, or a moment outside Temporal's range of -271821-04-19T00:00:00.000000001 to +275760-09-13T23:59:59.999999999. |
| `readonly calendarId: string` | The calendar, always `iso8601`. |
| `readonly day: i32` | The day of the month, from 1. |
| `readonly dayOfWeek: i32` | The weekday, 1 for Monday to 7 for Sunday. |
| `readonly dayOfYear: i32` | The day of the year, 1 for 1 January. |
| `readonly daysInMonth: i32` | Days in this date's month. |
| `readonly daysInWeek: i32` | Days in a week: 7. |
| `readonly daysInYear: i32` | Days in this date's year: 365 or 366. |
| `readonly hour: i32` | The hour, 0 to 23. |
| `readonly inLeapYear: boolean` | Whether this date's year is a leap year. |
| `readonly microsecond: i32` | The microsecond, 0 to 999. |
| `readonly millisecond: i32` | The millisecond, 0 to 999. |
| `readonly minute: i32` | The minute, 0 to 59. |
| `readonly month: i32` | The month, 1 to 12. |
| `readonly monthCode: string` | The month as Temporal codes it: `M01` to `M12`. |
| `readonly monthsInYear: i32` | Months in a year: 12. |
| `readonly nanosecond: i32` | The nanosecond, 0 to 999. |
| `readonly second: i32` | The second, 0 to 59. |
| `readonly weekOfYear: i32` | The ISO week number, 1 to 53. |
| `readonly year: i32` | The year. |
| `readonly yearOfWeek: i32` | The year the ISO week belongs to. |
| `add(duration: Duration): PlainDateTime` | This date-time moved by `duration`: the time fields first, carrying whole days, then the years and months with the day constrained to the new month, then the weeks, the days and the carried days — Temporal's AddDurationToDateTime. Panics with a `RangeError` outside Temporal's range. |
| `equals(other: PlainDateTime): boolean` | Whether `other` is the same date-time. |
| `since(other: PlainDateTime): Duration` | The time from `other` to this date-time: `other.until(this)`. |
| `subtract(duration: Duration): PlainDateTime` | This date-time moved back by `duration`: `add` of its negation. |
| `toJSON(): string` | The same string as `toString`. |
| `toPlainDate(): PlainDate` | The date part. |
| `toPlainTime(): PlainTime` | The time part. |
| `toString(): string` | The date-time as Temporal writes it: `2024-01-15T09:05:00`, with the fraction of the second to as many digits as it needs. |
| `until(other: PlainDateTime): Duration` | The time from this date-time to `other` in days and smaller units (Temporal's default `largestUnit: "day"`), every field with one sign. |
| `withPlainTime(time: PlainTime): PlainDateTime` | This date-time with its time replaced by `time`. |

### PlainTime

A time of day with no date and no time zone: `Temporal.PlainTime`.

```ts
class PlainTime
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new PlainTime(hour: i32 = 0, minute: i32 = 0, second: i32 = 0, millisecond: i32 = 0, microsecond: i32 = 0, nanosecond: i32 = 0)` | The time `hour:minute:second.millisecond microsecond nanosecond`, as `new Temporal.PlainTime(...)`; every field defaults to 0, so `new PlainTime()` is midnight. Panics with a `RangeError` on a field out of range. |
| `readonly hour: i32` | The hour, 0 to 23. |
| `readonly microsecond: i32` | The microsecond, 0 to 999. |
| `readonly millisecond: i32` | The millisecond, 0 to 999. |
| `readonly minute: i32` | The minute, 0 to 59. |
| `readonly nanosecond: i32` | The nanosecond, 0 to 999. |
| `readonly second: i32` | The second, 0 to 59. |
| `add(duration: Duration): PlainTime` | This time moved by the time fields of `duration`, wrapping past midnight; the years, months, weeks and days are ignored, as Temporal ignores them. |
| `equals(other: PlainTime): boolean` | Whether `other` is the same time. |
| `since(other: PlainTime): Duration` | The time from `other` to this time: `other.until(this)`. |
| `subtract(duration: Duration): PlainTime` | This time moved back by `duration`: `add` of its negation. |
| `toJSON(): string` | The same string as `toString`. |
| `toString(): string` | The time as Temporal writes it: `09:05:00`, with the fraction of the second to as many digits as it needs (`09:05:00.25`). |
| `until(other: PlainTime): Duration` | The time from this time to `other` on the same day, in hours and smaller units (Temporal's default `largestUnit: "hour"`). |
